gantry — GitGate eligibility checks (plan §\"Phase 0.5\", Components §3 \"GitGate\").\n//\n// Phase 0.5 walking skeleton, stage 2 of 5 (bf-3a7): builds on stage 1 (bf-6d4) shim\n// dispatch + Config::hardcoded() and adds the eligibility gate that decides a run\n// MAY go remote. This is the happy-path skeleton: the four checks run in order,\n// each shelling out to system git (no libgit2 — matches predecessor behavior), and\n// any failure returns a simple (eligible=false, reason). Full per-check reason\n// strings, untracked-file nuance, and topology edge cases are Phase 1a (bf-4zh).\n//\n// No RunLog, no decision integration yet — just the gate function + tests.\n\nuse std::process::Command;\n\n/// Eligibility result from GitGate.\n///\n/// The happy path is `eligible=true`; any failed check yields `eligible=false`\n/// with a simple reason string. Phase 1a will expand each reason to specific,\n/// actionable diagnostics (bf-4zh).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct Eligibility {\n    /// True iff all four GitGate checks passed.\n    pub eligible: bool,\n    /// Human-readable reason when ineligible; empty string when eligible.\n    pub reason: String,\n}\n\nimpl Eligibility {\n    /// The happy-path result: all checks passed.\n    fn eligible() -> Self {\n        Eligibility {\n            eligible: true,\n            reason: String::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// A failed check: ineligible with a simple reason.\n    fn ineligible(reason: &str) -> Self {\n        Eligibility {\n            eligible: false,\n            reason: reason.to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check whether cwd is inside a git work tree.\n///\n/// Runs `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` and returns true iff the output\n/// is \"true\". This is the first GitGate check (plan Components §3 \"GitGate\").\n/// Shells out to system git; never uses libgit2 (predecessor behavior contract).\nfn is_inside_work_tree() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"rev-parse\", \"--is-inside-work-tree\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git rev-parse failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    Ok(stdout.trim() == \"true\")\n}\n\n/// Check whether HEAD resolves.\n///\n/// Runs `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` and returns true iff it succeeds (exit\n/// code 0). This catches repos with no commits (HEAD unborn) and other malformed\n/// states. Shells out to system git; never uses libgit2.\nfn head_resolves() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"rev-parse\", \"--verify\", \"HEAD\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git rev-parse failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    Ok(output.status.success())\n}\n\n/// Check whether a configured remote exists.\n///\n/// Runs `git remote get-url <ci_remote>` and returns true iff it succeeds.\n/// The remote name comes from `config.ci_remote` (default: \"origin\"). Shells out\n/// to system git; never uses libgit2.\nfn remote_exists(ci_remote: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"remote\", \"get-url\", ci_remote])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git remote failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    Ok(output.status.success())\n}\n\n/// Check whether the working tree is clean (no uncommitted changes).\n///\n/// Runs `git status --porcelain` and returns true iff the output is empty.\n/// An empty output means no tracked files have changes and no untracked files\n/// are present (vanilla porcelain mode; Phase 1a adds untracked-file nuance).\n/// Shells out to system git; never uses libgit2.\nfn is_tree_clean() -> Result<bool, String> {\n    let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n        .args([\"status\", \"--porcelain\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"git status failed: {e}\"))?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\n            \"git status --porcelain failed: {}\",\n            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    Ok(stdout.trim().is_empty())\n}\n\n/// Run all four GitGate eligibility checks in order and return the result.\n///\n/// The checks run sequentially (plan Components §3 \"GitGate\"), stopping at the\n/// first failure:\n///\n/// 1. Inside a work tree (`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`)\n/// 2. HEAD resolves (`git rev-parse --verify HEAD`)\n/// 3. Configured remote exists (`git remote get-url <ci_remote>`)\n/// 4. Clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty)\n///\n/// The happy path (all four pass) yields `eligible=true`. Any failed check yields\n/// `eligible=false` with a simple reason string. Phase 1a (bf-4zh) expands each\n/// reason to specific, actionable diagnostics and adds untracked-file nuance.\n///\n/// This function only answers the eligibility question; it does not integrate\n/// with the decision engine, RunLog, or any pipeline stage. Integration lands\n/// in later beads.\npub fn check_git_gate(ci_remote: &str) -> Eligibility {\n    // Check 1: inside a work tree. If we're not even in a git repo, nothing\n    // else makes sense — fail fast with a clear reason.\n    match is_inside_work_tree() {\n        Ok(true) => {}\n        Ok(false) => return Eligibility::ineligible(\"not inside a git work tree\"),\n        Err(e) => panic!(\"GitGate check 1 failed: {e}\"),\n    }\n\n    // Check 2: HEAD resolves. Catches repos with no commits (HEAD unborn) and\n    // other malformed states.\n    match head_resolves() {\n        Ok(true) => {}\n        Ok(false) => return Eligibility::ineligible(\"HEAD does not resolve (no commits?)\"),\n        Err(e) => panic!(\"GitGate check 2 failed: {e}\"),\n    }\n\n    // Check 3: configured remote exists. The ci_remote (default \"origin\") must\n    // be configured or we have nowhere to push epoch refs.\n    match remote_exists(ci_remote) {\n        Ok(true) => {}\n        Ok(false) => {\n            return Eligibility::ineligible(&format!(\"remote '{ci_remote}' not configured\"))\n        }\n        Err(e) => panic!(\"GitGate check 3 failed: {e}\"),\n    }\n\n    // Check 4: clean tree. &std::path::Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String> {\n        let output = Command::new(\"git\")\n            .current_dir(dir)\n            .args(args)\n            .output()\n git repo with one commit and an 'origin' remote.\n    ///\n    /// This is the happy-path fixture: a committed-clean repo with a configured\n    /// remote that passes all four GitGate checks.\n    fn .output()\n            .expect(\"git init bare remote failed\");\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            panic!(\n                \"git init --bare failed: {}\",\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Initialize the main repo\n        git_cmd(repo_dir.path(), &[\"init\"]).expect(\"git init\");\n        git_cmd(repo_dir.path(), &[\"config\", \"user.name\", \"Test User\"])\n            .expect(\"git config user.name\");\n        git_cmd(\n            repo_dir.path(),\n            &[\"config\", \"user.email\", \"test@example.com\"],\n        )\n        .expect(\"git config user.email\");\n\n        // Add origin remote pointing at the bare repo\n        let remote_url = gantry — command-template backend (plan §\"Phase 0.5\", Components §5 \"RemoteBackend trait\").\n//\n// Phase 0.5 walking skeleton, stage 4 of 5 (bf-2vr): builds on stages 1-3 (shim/config\n// + GitGate + RefPusher) and implements the command-template backend that runs a\n// bash executor on the same box.\n//\n// The command backend implements RemoteBackend using hardcoded argv arrays:\n// - submit: runs the bash executor with the repo/sha/args, captures stdout as handle\n// - logs: stub (panics if called)\n// - wait: runs the bash executor with the handle, returns exit code -> verdict\n//\n// Phase 1a will make the argv arrays configurable via config file; the skeleton\n// uses hardcoded paths to contrib/gantry-exec.sh.\n\nuse crate::backend::{BackendError, RemoteBackend, RunHandle, RunSpec, Verdict};\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::process::{Command, Output};\nuse std::time::Instant;\n\n/// The command-template backend implementation.\n///\n/// Phase 0.5: hardcoded executor path at `./contrib/gantry-exec.sh`. The backend\n/// runs this script with argv-style arguments:\n///\n/// Submit (stores the run and emits a handle on stdout):\n///   contrib/gantry-exec.sh submit <repo_url> <sha> <args_json>\n///\n/// Wait (polls the run and exits with the run's exit code):\n///   contrib/gantry-exec.sh wait <handle>\n///\n/// Phase 1a will make these argv arrays configurable via config file templates.\npub struct CommandBackend {\n    /// Path to the bash executor script.\n    executor: String,\n}\n\nimpl CommandBackend {\n    /// Create a new CommandBackend with the hardcoded executor path.\n    ///\n    /// Phase 0.5: the executor is `./contrib/gantry-exec.sh` (relative to the\n    /// current working directory, which is the repo root for the skeleton).\n    /// The path can be overridden via the GANTRY_EXEC_PATH environment variable\n    /// for testing or alternative configurations.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        // Check for GANTRY_EXEC_PATH environment variable first (for testing)\n        let executor = std::env::var(\"GANTRY_EXEC_PATH\")\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"./contrib/gantry-exec.sh\".to_string());\n\n        CommandBackend { executor }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new CommandBackend with a custom executor path (for testing).\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn with_executor(executor: &str) -> Self {\n        CommandBackend {\n            executor: executor.to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Run the executor with arguments and return its output.\n    fn run_executor(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<Output, BackendError> {\n        Command::new(&self.executor)\n            .args(args)\n            .output()\n            .map_err(|e| BackendError::new(&format!(\"failed to run executor: {}\", e)))\n    }\n\n    /// Parse args JSON into a Vec<String> for the executor.\n    ///\n    /// Phase 0.5: use a simple JSON array format. The args are passed as a JSON\n    /// array of strings; the executor parses this and forwards each element to\n    /// the command (e.g., cargo test).\n    ///\n    /// Phase 1a will use serde_json for robust JSON handling.\n    fn format_args_json(args: &[String]) -> String {\n        // Phase 0.5: simple JSON array encoding\n        // This is a minimal implementation that works for simple cases\n        let parts: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(|a| a.as_str()).collect();\n        format!(\"[{}]\", parts.join(\",\"))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for CommandBackend {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RemoteBackend for CommandBackend {\n    /// Submit a run to the executor.\n    ///\n    /// Runs: `contrib/gantry-exec.sh submit <repo_url> <sha> <args_json>`\n    ///\n    /// The executor's stdout is the handle (an opaque string that wait() can use).\n    /// The skeleton expects the handle to be a single line of text (whitespace trimmed).\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns Err if:\n    /// - The executor binary cannot be run\n    /// - The executor exits non-zero (submit failure)\n    /// - The executor emits no output on stdout\n    fn submit(&self, spec: &RunSpec) -> Result<RunHandle, BackendError> {\n        let args_json = Self::format_args_json(&spec.args);\n\n        let output = self.run_executor(&[\"submit\", &spec.repo_url, &spec.sha, &args_json])?;\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            return Err(BackendError::new(&format!(\n                \"executor submit failed: {}\",\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)\n            )));\n        }\n\n        let handle = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n        if handle.is_empty() {\n            return Err(BackendError::new(\"executor emitted empty handle\"));\n        }\n\n        Ok(RunHandle::new(&handle))\n    }\n\n    /// Stream logs from the running run.\n    ///\n    /// Phase 0.5: not implemented — panics if called.\n    /// Phase 1a will implement log streaming for the command backend.\n    fn stream_logs(&self, h: &RunHandle, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<(), BackendError> {\n        let _ = (h, out);\n        panic!(\"stream_logs is not implemented in Phase 0.5\");\n    }\n\n    /// Wait for the run to complete and return its verdict.\n    ///\n    /// Runs: `contrib/gantry-exec.sh wait <handle>`\n    ///\n    /// The executor exits with the same exit code as the run it executed. The\n    /// backend maps this exit code to a Verdict using the minimal ladder:\n    /// - 0 -> Pass\n    /// - nonzero -> TestFailure\n    ///\n    /// ## Parameters\n    ///\n    /// - `h`: The RunHandle returned by submit().\n    /// - `deadline`: The deadline for the run (ignored in Phase 0.5 — the executor\n    ///   manages its own timeout). Phase 1a will enforce this at the backend level.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns Err if:\n    /// - The executor binary cannot be run\n    /// - The executor crashes (not the run itself, but the executor script)\n    /// - The handle is invalid or the run is not found\n    fn wait(&self, h: &RunHandle, _deadline: Instant) -> Result<Verdict, BackendError> {\n        let output = self.run_executor(&[\"wait\", &h.handle])?;\n\n        // The executor's exit code is the run's exit code\n        let exit_code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n\n        // Map to verdict using the minimal ladder\n        Ok(Verdict::from_exit_code(exit_code))\n    }\n\n    /// Describe the run for human consumption.\n    ///\n    /// Phase 0.5: not implemented — panics if called.\n    /// Phase 1a will return the handle or a configured URL template.\n    fn describe(&self, h: &RunHandle) -> String {\n        let _ = h;\n        panic!(\"describe is not implemented in Phase
